channel.title: Block Club Chicago - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Block Club Chicago (blockclubchicago.org)

item.title: Families Scammed By Convicted Mortgage Fraudsters Are Still Fighting For Their Homes
item.description: More than two decades after Mark Diamond began conning homeowners on the West and South sides, some of his victims have lost their homes, while others are battling lenders in court.

item.title: Find Your Fellow Haters At These Chicago Anti-Valentine’s Day Events
item.description: You can find a variety of fun Valentine’s-related events for the non-romantic all across the city.

item.title: Belmont Tavern, Dormant For 25 Years, Is Reborn In Avondale
item.description: The drink menu features 26 cocktails picked from owner Nick Kokonas’ bartending back catalog. Old Style is the only beer on draft.

item.title: After Years Of Population Loss, South Chicago Unites To Plan For A Brighter Future
item.description: Residents and community groups unveiled their latest plan to guide the neighborhood's development, capping off a year-long effort to draft the plan — and kicking off a years-long effort to implement it.

item.title: DePaul Students Push For ‘Sanctuary Campus’ Policies After Immigration Agents Spotted Nearby
item.description: Students want limits on cooperation with federal immigration agents, real-time alerts and formal policies they say would better protect immigrant and international classmates.

item.title: Chicago Sees Longest Winter Freeze In 19 Years — But Relief Is Coming
item.description: Temperatures have remained below freezing in Chicago since Jan. 16, but a warmup arrives Thursday and Friday.

item.title: Another Sip & Savor Appears To Have Closed, This Time In The South Loop
item.description: This would be the second closure in recent months for the local coffee chain. Three locations remain open.

item.title: After Feds Denied Him Lifesaving Meds, Hyde Park Man Ordered Released From ‘Unlawful’ Detention
item.description: Albeiro Ropero Remolina — who was arrested near his Hyde Park home in December and denied several doses of needed medication while in custody, according to his attorneys — was released on bond and returned home Monday.

item.title: Woman Sentenced To Prison For Hate Crime Over Assault And Defacing Of Pro-Palestinian Mural
item.description: Danielle Wasserman, 37, was sentenced Friday to a year in prison over two counts of a hate crime for assaulting two neighbors and vandalizing a Pro-Palestinian mural in Pilsen.

item.title: Should Food Delivery Robots Be Allowed In Wicker Park And Logan Square? Alderman Wants Input
item.description: Ald. Daniel La Spata’s office is seeking neighbors' opinions on whether or not the companies piloting the program should roll out the robots to the entire 1st Ward.
